entries.question: what is the eval resolution every decision is standardised by?

resolution.charter_cite: the sideways formation campaign's CHARTER.md:227 -- paired episode bootstraps, n=100: completion +-0.06..0.10, walking tripod +-0.016..0.056

decision_rule.text: F block = facing on turn_l90, turn_r90, move_turn: the per-episode closed fraction clip(1 - final/max(initial, 0.15), -1, 1) (None = uninformative when initial < 0.15) and the signed yaw_progress_rate; T block = speed_ratio on fwd, lat_l, diag, back; guards (four) = completion, tripod_walking_dir (min over the four direction holds), turn_survival_l90 = surv[turn_l90]/surv[back] and turn_survival_r90 = surv[turn_r90]/surv[turn_l90] (falls DURING the turns, not the cumulative survivals nested inside completion; a conditional survival is MISSING when its denominator is 0 or unavailable, and the bootstrap drops zero-denominator resamples). WATCH, never scored: track_ratio_tail (the training-log ratio includes the ~20 % move+turn rows, so a successful facing fix lowers it by design), the slot-gated track_ratio_move_tail, dir_ratio[move_turn], tripod_by_hold[move_turn], settle, right-handed holds, the cumulative survivals. One standardiser everywhere: R_i = R_eval,i, the metric's D00 paired-bootstrap half-width, never re-fitted. Block statistic z_F = mean_i(delta_i / R_i) (a closed fraction and a rad/s rate weigh equally); block resolution R_F = max(R_F^eval, R_F^seed) where R_F^eval is the paired-bootstrap 95 % half-width of z_F itself and R_F^seed is the block-level seed term of decision 6 -- likewise R_T and the two absolute-units blocks; guards one-sided at 99 % on their own per-metric R (max(R_eval,i, R_seed,i) single-seed). Null candidate all-TIE ~= 0.95^2 x 0.99^4 ~= 0.87 under eval noise (pinned), and B0_s2 submitted against B0_s3 is TIE on both blocks and every guard by construction (pinned). Per block: BETTER if z > R, WORSE if z < -R, else TIE. Clear ADOPT = >= 1 block BETTER, no WORSE (blocks or guards), and anchored drift OK; clear REJECT = any WORSE, or a FLOOR gate (a MISSING metric never blocks a REJECT); UNCERTAIN = all TIE -> speculative pick = the candidate's speculative_default when declared (C1c: candidate), else the sign of z_F + z_T (exact tie -> incumbent), notify, pair queued. Anchored drift (z of candidate vs anchor >= -R on both blocks and every guard) is a precondition of ANY ADOPT, clear or speculative, s3 or pooled -- a clear-ADOPT screen that fails it is recorded confidence: uncertain (evidence.anchored_drift: FAIL), status speculative, pick REJECT, and queues the pair exactly like an all-TIE UNCERTAIN; at the pooled level drift = the candidate's two-seed mean deltas vs the anchor's s3 (and its s2, paired seed-wise, when the anchor recipe has an ok s2 screen) at R_F^pooled/R_pooled,i, and a pooled drift pass with a pooled clear ADOPT is an ADOPT (a different pick -> self-overrule as usual). MISSING in a guard -> a decided REJECT (TERMINAL) with confidence: uncertain, evidence.missing: [<guards>] + WATCH and NO pair (a pair cannot supply the metric; decide --choose run re-runs the candidate later); MISSING in F/T -> that metric leaves the block mean and the best outcome is a speculative ADOPT. Absolute-units candidates (C3a, C3b -- any candidate that changes the command cap/clip or, if ever added, the speed ellipse): F = facing_closed + whole-hold net_yaw_rate_toward, T = achieved_vx m/s.

null-candidate check on 1c-004 @slow__omni (N=1000, two independent episode resamples per trial): all-TIE 0.888 with R re-derived on the same resample distribution (blocks F 0.953, T 0.962), 0.851 under D00's cross-head R

degenerate pair on turn_survival_r90: its cross-head R 0.0282 is at or below the perfectly-correlated floor of the same-run spread (0.0449/sqrt2 = 0.0318), i.e. one side of every pair is effectively constant on it, so the paired difference carries only the other side's variation. A null candidate then trips this guard more often than its level says (measured null TIE 0.949 under this R vs 0.994 under the calibrated one). Decision 6's max(R_eval, R_seed) from D00b is the mitigation -- watch it at window 2.

entries.question: what turn rate can this plant actually deliver?

turn_rate.note: the commanded cap is ~2x the plant's estimated turn ceiling, and the move+turn slot is infeasible at any commandable speed (walk floor 0.21 m/s => omega <= 0.01 rad/s at r_foot 1.2 m) -- so move+turn is scored relatively and every cap candidate is screened directly instead of probed

entries.question: what track_ratio_mean does a forming walker reach by iteration 1000 here?

evidence.rule: max(0.35, 0.75 x the baseline's own its-800-1000 mean)

entries.question: how much do two seeds of the SAME recipe differ?

Does the user's additive capability curriculum (one command type at a time, floor shares kept, move+turn ramped 0.10 -> 0.15 -> 0.20) buy facing AND translation over the single-stage incumbent at the same 8000 iterations? CONFOUND: c4-c6 draw world-held move+turn at the 0.3 rad/s cap, which the plant cannot deliver at any commandable speed (caveat 1) -- C1b re-screens with a 70 % smaller turn demand and C1c separates the pool from the staging.

entries.question: Attribution of an adopted curriculum: was it the POOL (all types at c6's mix for the whole window) or the STAGING (one type at a time)? On all-TIE the simpler recipe is the speculative pick (Occam) and the confirming pair still runs. Its chain's own seed resolution is D00c-scratch_c6.
